Requirement Jira: Description=Estimation: Analysis: 1-2 days DEV: 1-2 days QA: 4-5 Update to logic in place to generate templates for ICPs even when there is a status of "confirmation needed" for ICPs in the MHK system. This was discussed during review of QASTM-1832. Lisa Boldin is business contact for this request as well. Thank you! User Story - Ticket - 10/31/25 - Priority High [QASTM-1908] ICP: Update Triggering Logic to generate ICPs when there is status of "confirmation needed" - RITM0019531 - Express Scripts Jira Lead: Lisa Boldin / English Distefano Need By: NA Bus Reqt’s: 1/28/26 Final Reqt's: Qual Apps Inital Review: 1/28/26 Business Request (What): Update to logic in place to generate templates for ICPs even when there is a status of "confirmation needed" for ICPs in the MHK system Problem Statement (Why): ICPs were not triggering when there were ICPs in the MHK system with a status of “Confirmation needed”. A lot of times these ICPs are never mailed and stay in a confirmation needed status, as a back up we would still want a quality ICP to trigger. Future State/Description (How): Update logic for quality ICPs to still trigger even if there is a manual ICP in the system with the status of confirmation needed in MHK. Additional Information This was mostly during the Conduent outage but in the event, there is a system failed with our mailing vendor again or other system failure within MHK, we would like as a fail safe a quality ICP to trigger so that we can remain compliance with timeliness ICP mailing to the member. MHK Impact: Assumption is no as it is in addition to current logic in place - to confirm Acceptance Criteria: A: Member is due for a ICP per current logic B: If there is no ICP, then trigger quality ICP C: Additionally, if there is an ICP in the MHK system with a correspondence status of confirmation needed, then trigger a quality ICP. kc ‌

Creating a *Jira Service Desk* (now officially called {*}Jira Service Management{*}) is a fairly straightforward process, but the _right_ setup depends on what you want to support (IT, HR, internal requests, customers, etc.). Below is a clear, practical, step-by-step guide, including best practices so you don’t end up reworking it later.
----
h2. 1. Decide What Type of Service Desk You Need

Before touching Jira, be clear on {*}purpose and scope{*}.

Common examples:
* *IT Service Desk* – incidents, access requests, hardware/software
* *Internal Services* – HR, finance, facilities, onboarding
* *Customer Support* – external users, tickets via email or portal

Key questions:
* Who will *submit requests* (employees, customers, both)?
* Who will *work tickets* (agents, SMEs, third parties)?
* Do you need {*}SLAs{*}, approvals, or compliance tracking?

{quote}✅ Tip: Start with *one service desk* and expand later—Jira scales well.
{quote}
----
h2. 2. Get Access and Licensing Sorted

You’ll need:
* *Jira Service Management license*
* *Admin permissions* (Global Admin or Site Admin)

Roles to understand:
* *Agents* – licensed users who work tickets
* *Customers* – free users who submit requests
* *Admins* – configure workflows, fields, SLAs

{quote}✅ Customers are {*}unlimited and free{*}—no license impact.
{quote}
----
h2. 3. Create the Service Desk Project

In Jira:
# Go to *Projects → Create project*
# Select *Jira Service Management*
# Choose a template (common ones):
** IT Service Management
** General Service Management
** HR Service Management
# Name the project and choose a key (e.g., ITSD, HELP, HR)

This creates:
* Default workflows (Incident, Request, Change)
* A customer portal
* Basic SLAs
* Standard request types

----
h2. 4. Configure Request Types (Very Important)

Request types are what users see on the {*}portal{*}.

Examples:
* “Request New Laptop”
* “Report a System Outage”
* “Access to Application”

Steps:
# Go to *Project settings → Request types*
# Create or edit request types
# Map each request type to an *issue type*
# Customize the form fields:
** Keep it short
** Only ask what’s needed to triage
** Use dropdowns where possible

{quote}✅ Best practice: Aim for *5–15 request types* max initially.
{quote}
----
h2. 5. Customize Workflows

Workflows control ticket states.

Typical flow:

{{Open → In Progress → Waiting for Customer → Resolved → Closed}}
Where to configure:
* *Project settings → Workflows*
* Clone default workflows before editing

Add statuses for:
* Approvals
* Vendor waiting
* On hold
* Escalated issues

{quote}✅ Keep workflows simple. Over-engineering is the #1 Jira mistake.
{quote}
----
h2. 6. Set Up SLAs (Service Level Agreements)

SLAs measure response and resolution time.

Common SLAs:
* Time to First Response
* Time to Resolution

Steps:
# Go to *Project settings → SLAs*
# Define goals by:
** Priority
** Request type
** Business hours
# Add pause conditions (e.g., “Waiting for Customer”)

Example:
* High priority incident: 1h response, 4h resolution
* Low priority request: 1 business day response

----
h2. 7. Configure the Customer Portal

The portal is what customers interact with.

Customize:
* Portal name & welcome message
* Categories (Hardware, Software, Access)
* Knowledge base integration (Confluence)

Where:
* *Project settings → Portal settings*

{quote}✅ Clear language > Jira terminology. Avoid internal jargon.
{quote}
----
h2. 8. Set Notifications & Automation

Make the system work for you.

Notifications:
* Customer auto-replies
* Status change updates
* Resolution emails

Automation rules (examples):
* Auto-assign tickets by request type
* Escalate priority if SLA is close to breach
* Auto-close after X days resolved

Location:
* *Project settings → Automation*

----
h2. 9. Reporting & Dashboards

Track performance and bottlenecks.

Useful reports:
* SLA success rate
* Requests by type
* Agent workload
* Time to resolution

You can:
* Use built-in reports
* Create dashboards with gadgets
* Export data if needed

----
h2. 10. Test Before Launch

Before going live:
* Submit test tickets as a *customer*
* Validate SLAs trigger correctly
* Ensure emails/firewalls allow Jira emails
* Get feedback from agents and users

{quote}✅ Pilot with a small group first (1–2 weeks).
{quote}
----
h2. 11. Go Live & Improve

After launch:
* Watch request volume trends
* Monitor unused request types
* Adjust SLAs and workflows quarterly
* Add a knowledge base to reduce tickets

----

If you want, I can:
* Help choose the *right template* for your use case
* Design *request types* and workflows
* Recommend *SLAs* based on industry norms
* Create a *starter configuration checklist*
